Works Well - There are times when the ice maker on the refrigerator can't keep up with our ice needs. Usually that's when we're entertaining or going out and taking the cooler somewhere. It took about 2 hours to fill the ice basket. This isn't something you can just start doing to get a lot of ice right away. However, if you plan in advance, it should be fine. We will start making ice the night before it's needed then bag it up and put it in the freezer. I love that this maker recycles the melted water. That's a great idea! While it is noisy, it's more of a white noise than anything else. We found it to not be distracting. We like the shapes of the ice cubes. My husband thought it would be nice if the front of the maker was see through so you could see how much ice you have without having to peer down into it. Overall, this works well and makes decent ice cubes.

Small capacity, spotty performance - I purchased this exact washing machine about 2 years ago from a different Website. It was considerably cheaper than it is right now on Amazon. So for 2 years I really enjoyed it and with the exception of water getting stuck inside the machine at the end of the cycle, I really had no problems with it. You really can't fit that much in so living by myself I would have to do at least one load day in the winter and one every other day in the summer. If you have heavy clothes like jeans or hoodies, I suggest putting in no more then two pair. The drainage hose it comes with is sub par at best and I definitely had to fix that about a year ago because it started to acquire holes. So after two years it would start making a ticking noise everytime it would drain, I checked the belts and they were fine and could never get a handle on what the problem was so I began pricing new machines that had larger tub's because I knew it was just a matter of time until the washer died. It finally died last week in the middle of a load, tub stopped spinning and although the timing was terrible I was excited to get something new. So I would say as a beginner compact washing machine this is definitely a good one although I would say performance seems to be spotty at times. I wouldn't pay more than a $130 for it. Not to mention this is the only place where I have found this wash machine still being sold so I'm pretty sure they've discontinued the model. Honestly if I was you I would go for something that holds more weight because that just opens up an entire world of possibilities.

That also means they don't release these particles into the tea water itself, and as a result you don't have to use a strainer.

The mesh on these is like the goldtone filter used for coffee makers since the 1980s or so. They keep particles out of the water.

What I'd like to see to make these better is hinged "wings" that flip up so the filters can be used over wider tea pots.

As it is, I need to buy both sizes depending on the opening of my various tea pots. If they had "wings" that flipped up until they were horizontal I wouldn't have to do that.

At any rate, they work great and it's great to not have to use a strainer when pouring tea.

These are currently the only tea strainers Grace Teas and Mark T. Wendell (where Julia Child bought her tea) offer for sale, and I'm sured they've tried just about every design out there before settling on these.

These are also much easier to clean up after using because the mesh is so fine particles don't get stuck in the mesh the way they do with tea balls.

The product could be improved with wings so it can be used in even wider opening tea pots,, and there's no need to use the lid when using in a tea pot (use the pot's lid instead), but other than that, there's nothing that performs better at keeping dust and fine particles off your counters and out of your water. Highly recommended.

The refrigerator is seven foot tall, forty-two inches wide, and nearly five hundred pounds empty, so the repair requires two appliance repair technicians to remove it from the cabinet so they can drill out the rivets - no simple screws here- panels from the back of the refrigerator, install a very expensive GE only part, re-rivet the rear panels into place, and do a 'fair' job re-caulking the interior panels that needed to be removed.

The data shared by both manufacturers is right there for even the cheapest, ahem, 'financially efficient,' health conscious user to see.
